transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Time: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 mins
Attendees: Jamie Lin (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Skyward Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Skyward Platform), Rachel Chen (Skyward Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Goal: scope a 6-week POC to validate Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted for Skyward's recommendation engine traffic shape.
- Key success criteria discussed: p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, model quality regression thresholds, security posture (VPC/KMS/SOC2).
- Data requested: 7 days of request logs, prompt families, SLO targets.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro: im jamie from Redwood, AE on this account. Marco my SE is on to do the workload and perf details.
[00:12] Priya: thanks, jamie. curious to see if Redwood handles our bursty retail traffic — we have spikes during flash sales and returns windows.
[00:19] Marco: totally. we've seen patterns like 10x bursts for short windows, also a long tail of low qps. want to capture both average qps and peak concurrency so we size the POC.
[00:30] Liam: to be concrete, avg qps is about 12/sec, baseline, with peaks up to ~140 qps during promos, lasting ~20-40s, more frequent during holidays.
[00:42] Priya: and typical prompt sizes are small-ish — about 20-40 input tokens, responses avg 120-220 tokens depending on personalization depth. some flows ask for reranks which increase token counts.
[00:55] Marco: ok that token mix matters. for cost and throughput we need distribution: percent of calls that are short replies vs long generative. also how often you call embeddings or reranking.
[01:08] Priya: embeddings are separate product, around 2% of traffic. re-ranks maybe 6% — most are single-turn recommendations.
[01:16] Jamie: success criteria recap — can you confirm p95 latency target and quality bar? we heard p95 sub-300ms for recommendation inference?
[01:26] Priya: right — p95 < 300ms is ideal for the core recommend endpoint. for batch/rerank it's ok to be higher, like < 1s. cost target — we're aiming for <$30 per 1M tokens processed, ballpark.
[01:40] Marco: noted. We'll aim benchmark runs for steady-state throughput to validate cost, and tail-latency tests for the bursts. We'll also test fallback policies — e.g., degrade to smaller model or cached response when latency creeps up.
[01:55] Liam: security is non-negotiable — we need VPC peering, KMS-managed keys, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. also SSO (SAML) for console access.
[02:07] Jamie: Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and KMS; we'll include SOC2 docs. we'll flag any on-prem requirements — do you anticipate air-gapped?
[02:16] Priya: not air-gapped, but strict data retention rules, and no raw prompt storage for more than 30 days.
[02:23] Marco: ok. for the POC we propose a 6-week plan: week 1 ingest logs and finalize traffic model, week 2 infra setup and baseline bench, week 3 brownfield runs for steady-state, week 4 burst testing and fallback policy tuning, week 5 quality evals and regression checks, week 6 polish and handover.
[02:41] Priya: that timeline aligns with our internal launch target. what about metrics for model quality — BLEU/Rouge arent great for recommender. we use CTR delta and downstream conversion.
[02:51] Marco: understood — we'll measure model fidelity by proxy metrics you define (CTR lift on held-out testset) and also do A/B style comparisons between model variants. we'll integrate with your telemetry for event-level correlation if you can provide sample logs.
[03:05] Rachel: from procurement perspective, we need an initial SOW and an estimate of costs for both Hosted and Dedicated options. and contract terms for provisioning reserved capacity if we go Dedicated.
[03:16] Jamie: we'll send a two-path SOW: 6-week POC for Hosted with a path to Dedicated (reserved pool sizing options and pricing). pricing ballparks in SOW; final numbers after bench runs.
[03:28] Priya: curious about the throughput math — you mentioned batching and KV cache earlier. does Redwood do prefix caching for repeated prompts?
[03:36] Marco: yes, we have prefix/KV caching and auto-batching. but caching effectiveness depends on prompt variability — if you have templated prompts caching helps a lot; highly personalized prompts less so. we can run a hit-rate estimate if you include prompt fingerprinting in the logs.
[03:52] Liam: our logs currently have hashed user ids and template ids, so that should be fine. we'll share schema.
[03:58] Marco: perfect. for benchmark shapes we plan to simulate: (1) steady state at avg qps = 12, (2) sustained 2x load for 10 minutes, (3) 10x burst for 30s every 5 minutes, and (4) tail stress test up to 200 qps to observe graceful degradation.
[04:18] Priya: and concurrency? our frontend can open up to ~120 concurrent connections during spikes.
[04:25] Marco: ok we'll model concurrency separately; batching helps reduce token-cost but increases latency variance, so we will test with continuous batching disabled and enabled to show tradeoffs.
[04:36] Jamie: any concerns around model variants — do you plan to use an open model family or a hosted proprietary one?
[04:42] Priya: we internally prefer open weights for cost control, but we might test a commercial model as fallback.
[04:48] Marco: good — we'll include compatibility tests across a small set of candidate models and provide kernel/quantization recommendations for your target hardware.
[04:57] Rachel: what do we need from legal/infra to start?
[05:00] Jamie: procurement: we'll include standard DPA and data handling appendix in the SOW. infra: VPC peering details and an IAM user for provisioning, plus KMS ARN.
[05:10] Priya: timeline check — if we get logs by 10/28, is a 6-week POC still realistic?
[05:15] Marco: yes, with a couple of caveats: quick access to logs and a prioritized set of ten core prompt families. otherwise week 1 slips.
[05:23] Priya: okay we'll prioritize that.
[05:25] Jamie: quick recap of open items and owners: we need logs + prompt taxonomy from Priya; SOW and pricing from me; rough infra sizing from Marco; and procurement to review SOW — Rachel.
[05:38] Liam: small note: during holiday season there's also a pattern of concurrent embeddings calls which spike our redis. will surface that in the logs.
[05:46] Marco: thanks — we'll watch for mixed workloads.
[05:49] Priya: thanks everyone. sounds good.
[05:52] Jamie: thanks all — we'll follow up with the SOW and the workload template.
